questions.q: A plane wave \(y=a \sin (\omega t-k x)\) propagates through a stretched string. The particle velocity versus \(x\) graph at \(t=0\) is
questions.solution: Plane wave is given as \(y=a \sin (\omega t-k x)\) at \(t=0\), \(\begin{aligned} & y=a \sin (\omega \times 0-k x) \\ & \Rightarrow \quad=a \sin (-k x) \Rightarrow-a \sin k x \\ \end{aligned}\) Particle velocity, \(\begin{aligned} v_{\mathrm{pa}} & =\frac{d y}{d t}=\frac{d}{d t}(-a \sin k x) \\ & =-a k \cos k x=-a k \cos \frac{2 \pi}{\lambda} x\left[\because k=\frac{2 \pi}{\lambda}\right] \\ & =-\frac{2 \pi a}{\lambda} \cos \frac{2 \pi x}{\lambda} \quad \ldots (i) \end{aligned}\) From Eq. (i), When \(x=0, v_{\mathrm{pa}}=\frac{-2 \pi a}{\lambda} \cdot \cos 0=\frac{-2 \pi a}{\lambda}\) When \(x=\frac{\lambda}{4}, v_{\mathrm{pa}}=\frac{-2 \pi a}{\lambda} \cdot \cos \frac{\pi}{2}=0\) When \(x=\frac{\lambda}{2}, v_{\mathrm{pa}}=\frac{-2 \pi a}{\lambda} \cdot \cos \pi=\frac{2 \pi a}{\lambda}\) When \(x=\frac{3 \lambda}{4}, v_{\mathrm{pa}}=\frac{-2 \pi a}{\lambda} \cos \left(\frac{-\pi}{2}\right)=0\) When \(x=\lambda, v_{\mathrm{pa}}=\frac{-2 \pi a}{\lambda} \cdot \cos 2 \pi=\frac{-2 \pi a}{\lambda}\) Hence, correct graph is

questions.q:
A source of sound emits sound waves at frequency $f_0$. It is moving towards an observer with fixed speed $v_s\left(v_s < v\right.$, where $v$ is the speed of sound in air.) If the observers were to move towards the source with speed $v_0$, one of the following two graphs $(A$ and $B)$ will give the correct variation of the frequency $f$ heard by the observer as $v_0$ is changed.

The variation of $f$ with $v_0$ is given correctly by
questions.solution:
According to Doppler's effect, the apparent frequency of sound when both source and observer are moving towards each other

\begin{array}{ll}
\Rightarrow & f=\frac{\left(v+v_0\right) f_0}{\left(v-v_0\right)} \\
\Rightarrow & f=\left(\frac{v}{v-v_s}\right) f_0+\left(\frac{v_0}{v-v_s}\right) f_0
\end{array}

\Rightarrow \quad f=\left(\frac{f_0}{v-v_s}\right) v_0+\left(\frac{f_0}{v-v_s}\right) v

Equation of straight line, $y=m x+c$ which is equation of straight line making an intercept $c$ on $Y$-axis, Slope of the graph $=\frac{f_0}{v-v_s}$ and intercept $=\frac{v f_0{ }^{\circ}}{v-v_s}$ This condition is represented in graph A plotted between $f$ and $v_0$.
Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.q: A train whistling at constant frequency $n$ is moving towards a station at a constant speed $v$. The train goes past a stationary observer on the station. The frequency $n$ of the sound as heard by the observer is plotted as a function of time $t$. Identify the correct curve.
questions.solution:
Since, the observer is stationary, so when train is approaching towards the observer or moving towards the observer, apparent frequency is given as,
$n^{\prime}=n\left(\frac{v}{v-v_{s}}\right)$
where, $v_{s}$ is the speed of sound.
It is clear from the above expression that $n^{\prime}>n$. However, when the train is going away from the observer, then apparent frequency,
$\begin{array}{ll} 
& n^{\prime}=n\left(\frac{v}{v+v_{s}}\right) \\
\therefore \quad & n^{\prime} < n
\end{array}
Hence, graph represented in option (d) is correct.

questions.q:
The figure below shows pressure variation in two different sound waves in air with time at a given position. Both the figures are drawn to the same scale.
Which of the following statements is true?
options: Wave 1 has lower frequency and smaller amplitude compared to wave 2
Wave 1 has higher frequency and greater amplitude compared to wave 2
Wave 1 has shroter wavelength and greater amplitude compared to wave 2
Wave 1 has shorter wavelength and smaller amplitude compared to wave 2
questions.solution:
Reason (brief):
- The graphs are \(P\) vs \(t\) at a fixed position and same scale.
- Wave 1 shows more oscillations in the same time \(\Rightarrow\) higher frequency than Wave 2.
- In the same medium, wave speed \(v\) is the same, so \(v=f \lambda \Rightarrow \lambda=\frac{v}{f}\). Hence higher \(f\) (Wave 1) \(\Rightarrow\) smaller \(\lambda\).
- The peak displacement from the mean (pressure amplitude) is smaller for Wave 1 than for Wave 2. Therefore, Wave 1: shorter wavelength and smaller amplitude \(\rightarrow\) option (4).

questions.q:
Assertion: In Doppler effect, if the source is moving, change in frequency is observed due to change in wavelength.
Reason : By the motion of source wavelength always decreases.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
If both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
If Assertion is true but Reason is false.
If Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
When the source moves, the wavelength of sound waves changes (compressed if source approaches, stretched if source recedes). Since velocity of sound in medium is constant, frequency changes as \(f= v / \lambda . \rightarrow\) Assertion is correct.
But wavelength does not always decrease, it decreases only when the source moves towards the observer, and increases if it moves away. \(\rightarrow\) Reason is incorrect.
Final Answer: Assertion is True, Reason is False.

"Longitudinal waves are called pressure waves."
\(\checkmark\) True - because compressions and rarefactions cause local pressure variations.
Reason:
"Propagation of longitudinal waves through a medium involves changes in pressure."

questions.q:
Assertion : Fundamental frequency of a narrow organ
pipe is more than a broad diameter organ pipe of same length.
Reason: If we apply Laplace end correction, then fundamental frequency of a closed organ pipe is more than v/4I.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
If both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
If Assertion is true but Reason is false.
If Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion: True. For the same physical length \(L\), a narrow pipe has smaller end correction than a broad pipe, so its effective length \(L_{\text {eff }}=L+e\) is smaller and therefore its fundamental frequency \(f \propto 1 / L_{\text {eff }}\) is larger.
Reason: False. Applying end correction increases the effective length, so the actual fundamental frequency is less than \(v /(4 L)\), not more. The Reason's statement is therefore incorrect.

If both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
If Assertion is true but Reason is false.
If Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution: Transverse waves need shear modulus, which air lacks (thereas only bulk modulus), Hence transverse waves cannot travel in air. Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason correctly explains Assertion.

questions.q:
Assertion: Doppler effect does not depend upon the distance between source and observer.
Reason: If source and observer are moving with same velocities, then no Doppler effect will be observed.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
If both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
If Assertion is true but Reason is false.
If Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion is correct. The Doppler effect (change in frequency) depends on the relative velocity between the source and the observer, not the distance between them.
Reason is correct. If the source and observer move with the same velocity in the same direction, their relative velocity is zero. Therefore, there is no Doppler shift.
The reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. The principle of relative velocity in the reason directly supports the assertion that distance is irrelevant.

Match List I with List II

A Troposphere I Approximate 65-75 km over Earth’s surface
B E-Part of Stratosphere II Approximate 300 km over Earth’s surface
C F2-Part of Thermosphere III Approximate 10 km over Earth’s surface

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
(A) The troposphere extends upward to about 10 km (6.2 miles or about 33,000 feet) above sea level. 

(B) The Electrical-layer or E-part of stratosphere lies approximately 100 km over Earth’s surface

(C) The F2-part of thermosphere lies approximately 300 km over Earth’s surface.

(D) D-part of Stratosphere lies approximate 65-75 km
 over Earth’s surface

Thus, A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

Source has frequency \(f\). Source and observer both have same speed. For the apparent frequency observed by observer, match the following columns.
\(\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|}
\hline & \text{Column I} & & \text{Column II} \\
\hline \text{(A)} & \begin{array}{l} \text{Observer is approaching} \\ \text{the source but source} \\ \text{is receding from the observer} \end{array} & \text{(p)} & \text{More than } f \\
\hline \text{(B)} & \begin{array}{l} \text{Observer and source} \\ \text{both approaching towards} \\ \text{each other} \end{array} & \text{(q)} & \text{Less than } f \\
\hline \text{(C)} & \begin{array}{l} \text{Observer and source} \\ \text{both receding from} \\ \text{each other} \end{array} & \text{(r)} & \text{Equal to } f \\
\hline \text{(D)} & \begin{array}{l} \text{Source is approaching} \\ \text{but observer is receding} \end{array} & \text{(s)} & \text{None} \\
\hline
\end{array}\)
options: \((A \rightarrow r, B \rightarrow p, C \rightarrow q, D \rightarrow r)\)
\((A \rightarrow p, B \rightarrow q, C \rightarrow s, D \rightarrow r)\)
\((A \rightarrow q, B \rightarrow r, C \rightarrow s, D \rightarrow r)\)
\((A \rightarrow s, B \rightarrow p, C \rightarrow q, D \rightarrow r)\)

questions.q:
A wave is transmitted from a denser to rarer medium. Then, match the following columns.
\(\begin{array}{l|l}
\hline \text{Column I} & \text{Column II} \\
\hline \text{(A) Frequency of wave} & \text{(p) Will increase} \\
\text{(B) Speed of wave} & \text{(q) Will decrease} \\
\text{(C) Wavelength of wave} & \text{(r) Will remain unchanged} \\
\text{(D) Amplitude of wave} & \text{(s) May increase or decrease} \\
\hline
\end{array}\)
questions.solution:
Frequency is the property of source. It remains unchanged.
In rarer medium, speed of wave is more.
Since,
\(\begin{gathered}
\lambda=\frac{v}{f} \text { or } \lambda \propto v \\
A_1=\left(\frac{2 v_2}{v_1+v_2}\right) A_i \\
v_2>v_1 \quad \therefore \quad A_i>A_i
\end{gathered}\)

\hline \text{(A)} & \begin{array}{l} \text{Temperature of gas} \\ \text{is made 4 times and} \\ \text{pressure 2 times} \end{array} & \text{(p)} & \text{Speed becomes 2 } \sqrt{2} \text{ times} \\
\hline \text{(B)} & \begin{array}{l} \text{Only pressure is made} \\ \text{4 times without change} \\ \text{in temperature} \end{array} & \text{(a)} & \text{Speed becomes 2 times} \\
\hline \text{(C)} & \begin{array}{l} \text{Only temperature is} \\ \text{changed to 4 times} \end{array} & \text{(r)} & \text{Speed remains unchanged} \\
\hline \text{(D)} & \begin{array}{l} \text{Molecular mass of the} \\ \text{gas is made 4 times} \end{array} & \text{(s)} & \text{Speed remains half} \\
\hline
\end{array}\)
options: \((A \rightarrow q, B \rightarrow r, C \rightarrow q, D \rightarrow s)\)
\((A \rightarrow r, B \rightarrow s, C \rightarrow q, D \rightarrow p)\)
\((A \rightarrow s, B \rightarrow p, C \rightarrow q, D \rightarrow r)\)
\((A \rightarrow p, B \rightarrow q, C \rightarrow r, D \rightarrow s)\)
questions.solution:
\(v=\sqrt{\frac{\gamma R T}{M}}=\sqrt{\frac{v p}{\rho}}\)
Speed does not change with change in pressure unless temperature is changed.

questions.q:
Following is given the equation of a travelling wave (all is SI units)
\(y=(0.02) \sin 2 \pi(10 t-5 x)\)
Match the following columns.
\(\begin{array}{l|l|l}
\hline \text{Column I} & \text{Column II} \\
\hline \text{(A) Speed of wave} & \text{(p) } 10 \\
\text{(B) Frequency of wave} & \text{(q) } 0.4 \pi \\
\text{(C) Wavelength of wave} & \text{(r) } 2 \\
\text{(D) Maximum particle speed} & \text{(s) } 0.2 \\
\hline
\end{array}\)
options: \((A \rightarrow r, B \rightarrow q, C \rightarrow s, D \rightarrow p)\)
\((A \rightarrow p, B \rightarrow r, C \rightarrow s, D \rightarrow q)\)
\((A \rightarrow r, B \rightarrow p, C \rightarrow s, D \rightarrow q)\)
\((A \rightarrow r, B \rightarrow q, C \rightarrow s, D \rightarrow p)\)
questions.solution:
Put wave in standard form \(y(x, t)=A \sin (\omega t-k x)\) (or \(A \sin (2 \pi f t-k x))\).
Read off amplitude \(\mathrm{A}\), angular frequency \(\mathrm{\omega}\) and wave number \(\mathrm{k}\).
Frequency: \(f=\frac{\omega}{2 \pi_\pi}\).
Wavelength: \(\lambda=\frac{2 \pi}{k}\).
Wave speed: \(v=\frac{\omega^{\prime}}{k}=f \lambda\).
Maximum particle speed: \(v_{\max }=A \omega\).
